newsitem.title: FRANCE: French PM Juppe visits his bombed mayoral office.
newsitem.headline: French PM Juppe visits his bombed mayoral office.

text.p: Prime Minister Alain Juppe toured his bombed mayoral offices in the French city of Bordeaux on Sunday as investigators said Corsican separatists might be responsible.

Hours after a powerful device damaged the elegant 18th century city hall, blowing out many windows but causing no casualties, the centre-right premier flew back from Paris under heavy escort but refused to speculate on the culprits.

Juppe, who had left his south-west France power-bse to fly to the capital some four hours before the blast late on Saturday, picked his way through the ornate reception hall -- a mess of broken glass, wrecked antique furniture, and paintings dashed to the ground.

The device blew up at 11.41 p.m. (2141 GMT) outside the hall where Juppe had met local officials on Saturday morning and where the south-western city was due to host a Franco-British summit in early November.

"I am not the kind of man who lets himself be intimidated. The rule of law will prevail," he told reporters, adding he would meet interior and justice ministers on Monday to discuss what measures should be taken.

Wood panelling suffered from the blast, as did the painted ceiling which sported large cracks. French windows leading out on the rear garden were blown out, but a massive crystal chandelier hanging from the ceiling escaped unharmed. The blast also damaged Juppe's own office.
"I heard an enormous explosion and then I saw a cloud of smoke in the sky," said one eye-witness.
Bordeaux prosecutor Patrice Davost said investigators had no idea of the make-up of the explosive, adding that they had received no threats beforehand or claims of responsibility.

Investigators said separatist guerrillas waging a long bombing campaign on the French Mediterranean island of Corsica might have planted the device, reportedly made up of plastic explosive or dynamite.

"Security measures were taken after the Prime Minister's speech on Corsica," one investigator said in reference to a crackdown decreed by Juppe this summer which prompted separatists to threaten attacks on the mainland.

The clandestine Corsican National Liberation Front - Historical Wing (FLNC) last week claimed responsibility for a bomb attack outside the law courts in Aix-en-Provence in southern France, the first on the mainland in several years.
Nationalist leaders have accused Juppe of blocking secret talks aimed at resolving their differences.

Charles Pieri, secretary-general of the Cuncolta movement which is close to the FLNC, said in June that "if the peace process does not succeed, the possibility of spreading the armed struggle to the mainland cannot be ruled out".
A wave of bombings, chiefly in Paris, hit France last year. The attacks were blamed on Moslem fundamentalists angered by France's support for Algerian authorities.
